central_claim.note: Lists interest, knowledge and online participation as examples, not as the strongest, so F1 is not credited here (as in the earlier judge's qwen note).

key_findings.note: States the positive association (quoting Expectation 1, which the results confirm, p.11) but not the strongest indicators.

flags.text: Reports Expectation 2 as a finding without qualification: stronger associations among more affectively polarized users. The paper finds this only partly, clearest for online and offline participation, 'partially consistent with Expectation 2 rather than a uniform confirmation' and exploratory for the remaining indicators (p.14).

key_findings.note: Greater activity and potential reach (wording kept from Expectation 3, so no flag); does not say more posts, followers and, less so, friends.

theoretical_positioning.note: Classical engagement theories (p.15). 'Extends' is credited partially as T3, as the earlier judge did for a near-identical qwen entry; the revisionist view is not named in the claim, only in the quote ('darker sides of engagement').

flags.text: Says the paper 'disputes the claim' that hostility is 'solely' associated with deprivation, marginalization or personality. Prior work is not quoted as claiming exclusivity; the paper 'does not seek to adjudicate between these literatures' (p.3) and presents engagement as an additional correlate ('not only', p.15).

interlocutor_claim.note: Grievance accounts (I3) with the paper's 'not only' content; the personality account is not specified as the small-segment, extreme-traits finding (I4 partial). Stance word tilts from 'adds to' to 'disputes'.
